title: Logistics implementation attestation
description: A source-neutral record that a client hub compiled an archetype against real sources and observed a specific canonical choice, grain, or cardinality. An attestation is evidence that may raise, corroborate, or force re-review of a registry concept — see validate_logistics_blueprint.py's evidence_basis check. It never by itself authorises disposition: approved. No client names, source-system names, or column names are permitted anywhere in this document, including the filename.

id.description: Opaque attestation id. MUST equal the YAML filename stem. Not a client identifier.

archetype.description: Archetype id (blueprints/archetypes/<id>.yaml) the attestation was gathered against.

accelerator.description: Accelerator pack id (accelerator-packs/<id>/) the attestation belongs to.

concept_id.description: Canonical registry concept id this observation bears on.

chosen_parent.description: Class IRI the implementation actually anchored on.

declined_parent.description: Class IRI the registry recommends, if different from chosen_parent. A declined_parent recurring across attestations forces re-review of that anchor.

decline_reason.description: Short, structural reason for declining the registry's recommended parent. No source-system or column names.

grain.description: One structural sentence describing the observed grain.

patterns_used.description: Ids of blueprints/patterns/<id> applied during this implementation.

grain_collisions_encountered.description: Short structural descriptions of source-noun-versus-grain collisions encountered, e.g. 'one source relation carried two distinct grains'. No source-system or column names.
